newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank to keep short-term rate target.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank to keep short-term rate target.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong pledged on Thursday to maintain the bank's target zone for short-term interest rates at 5.0-5.5 percent.
"We will maintain our short-term rate target zone at 5.0 to 5.5 percent," Sheu said during a day of parliament testimony.
The interbank rate typically trades in the bank's target zone, but recently has spiked above 8.0 percent. It had risen slightly and was hovering about 6.1 percent as Sheu spoke.
Sheu attributed the rate spikes mainly to strong demand for cash for the red-hot stock market, which has surged nearly 1,150 points or 16.6 percent in 1997 alone.
The stock index gained 0.77 percent on Thursday to close at 8,081.00 on frenzied turnover of T$174 billion.
